Your orders were simple.

Restore discipline. Secure the prisoners. Keep the dungeons in the service of Rondon.

You accepted the captaincy believing that a firm hand would be enough.

The guards were insubordinate. The priests refused to explain their work. Prisoners disappeared from locked cells, and the men responsible for counting them had stopped reporting the losses.

You began keeping a diary.

You recorded what you could not correct. The neglect. The cruelty. What Trortur had done to a child left in his care.

You considered having him arrested.

Instead, you avoided the torture chambers.

When the prisoner Le’garde arrived, the priests demanded custody. They intended to take him below the mines.

You objected. An order bearing the authority of your superiors settled the matter.

You handed him over.

That night, you dreamed of crows.

The dreams continued.

There were shapes moving behind the clouds. Patterns you almost understood. You would wake with the certainty that something had been explained to you, only to forget it before you could reach for your diary.

Soon, you began seeing the patterns while awake.

In the damp stone. In the arrangement of the bodies. In the movements of your own men.

You slept less.

For the first time since your arrival, the dungeons began to make sense.

You had mistaken the corruption for a failure of discipline.

It was deeper than that.

You could see it in everyone around you. The guards. The priests. The prisoners begging through their doors.

There was no one you could trust with the task.

You opened your diary one last time.

*I will start the purge.*

*I will root out the madness.*

*Only I can do it.*

You left your quarters without your uniform.

A length of cloth was enough. You would be going deep, and the passages were hot.

Someone called your name as you passed.

You kept walking.

You cannot remember how long you have been below.

One arm has grown heavy. Its weight feels useful.

You try to speak an order, but your mouth no longer makes the proper sounds.

It does not matter. No one here obeys orders.

Beyond a nearby door, you hear someone moving.

You have not inspected that room yet.
*A terrifying presence has entered the world…*
